subject: space
title: How Do Shadows Change During the Day?
question: Why is my shadow long in the morning and short at lunchtime?

steps.title: What is a shadow?
steps.text: Sunlight shines on the playground. When something is in the way, it blocks the light. The dark patch behind it, where the light cannot reach, is its shadow. The tree, the child and the stick each have one.
steps.try: Switch off 'Sunny day' so a cloud covers the Sun. Then switch it back on.
steps.see: With the Sun out, every shadow is sharp and dark. When a cloud covers the Sun, the shadows fade away.

steps.title: Light goes in straight lines
steps.text: Light travels in straight lines. It cannot bend around the stick. The yellow line is one ray of sunlight that just passes the top of the stick. The shadow ends where that ray reaches the ground.
steps.try: Move the time slider and follow the yellow ray.
steps.see: The Sun, the top of the stick and the end of the shadow are always in one straight line.

steps.title: Can light go through?
steps.text: A wooden board does not let light through, so it makes a dark shadow. Clear glass lets almost all the light through, so it makes only a very faint shadow. Things that light cannot pass through, like wood, stone and people, are called opaque.
steps.try: Compare the shadow of the wooden board with the shadow of the glass window.
steps.see: Behind the board there is a dark shadow. Behind the glass the ground is still bright, and only the wooden frame makes a shadow.

steps.title: Morning: long shadows
steps.text: In the morning the Sun rises in the east. It is low in the sky, so its light comes in from the side and shadows are very long. They point to the west, away from the Sun.
steps.try: Watch the Sun climb, or move the time slider from 6 o'clock to 10 o'clock.
steps.see: The higher the Sun climbs, the shorter the shadows get.

steps.title: Midday: short shadows
steps.text: Around the middle of the day the Sun is at its highest in the sky. Now shadows are at their shortest. In most places the Sun is not straight overhead, so there is still a small shadow.
steps.try: Move the time slider to find when the stick's shadow is the shortest.
steps.see: The shortest shadow comes around midday, when the Sun is highest. The shadow still points away from the Sun.

steps.title: A whole day of shadows
steps.text: In the afternoon the Sun sinks toward the west, and shadows grow long again, now pointing east. The Sun is not really travelling around us. The Earth is turning, as you saw in the Day and Night lesson, and that makes the Sun seem to cross the sky.
steps.try: Press Play the day. The red dots mark where the stick's shadow ended each hour.
steps.see: Shadows are long in the morning, short at midday and long again in the evening. They always point away from the Sun.

quiz.q: When is your shadow the shortest?
quiz.why: Around midday the Sun is highest in the sky, so shadows are shortest.

quiz.q: The Sun is low in the east. Which way does your shadow point?
options: To the east, toward the Sun
To the west, away from the Sun
quiz.why: A shadow is on the side away from the light, so with the Sun in the east it points west.

quiz.q: Which one makes the darkest shadow?
options: A clear plastic bottle of water
quiz.why: Wood is opaque: it lets no light through. Clear glass and clear plastic let most light pass.
